newsitem.title: UK: North Sea steady but sellers claim better bids.
newsitem.headline: North Sea steady but sellers claim better bids.

text.p: North Sea crudes traded at broadly unchanged levels on Thursday but some sellers said they detected improved interest for April barrels, particularly those with high gasoline yields.
March 29-31 Brent fetched April Brent -90 cents a barrel, worth a bearish May Brent -77 cents, but traders said most attention was switching to early April wet values.
British Petroleum now holds six of the seven April Brents which have turned wet so far, one of them taken in a "late pass" from Wall Street trader Aron who was clocked on Thursday.
Another April 4-6 stem was clocked to Phibro, traders said.
Brent paper markets were quiet, May gaining about six cents to $20.38 by 1830 GMT. Next week's CFDs traded twice at a slightly weaker May Brent -46 cents.
Forties was the pick of the North Sea grades, trading at Dated Brent +10 cents for a first decade loader, three cents firmer than on Wednesday, traders said.
News some refiners in northwest Europe were restoring crude runs to normal levels after recent reductions due to poor margins was providing mild support to differentials, they said.
In the Mediterranean, pressure on Urals eased a shade with the sale of Iraqi Kirkuk into northwest Europe.
Prompt and cross-month Urals were pegged at Dated Brent -$1.40/-$1.20 a barrel basis cif Augusta.

Syrian price talks for April reached a deadlock with Sytrol holding to its opening offer of Dated Brent -78 cents for Light crude, representing a cut of 28 cents on the March OSP. Heavy Souedie was offered at Dated Brent -$4.60 a barrel.
Much West African trade was shrouded by widespread insistence on confidential terms, with sellers unwilling to disclose apparently weak traded values.
Mid-April loaders were the main market for end-users but three unsold cargoes at the end of March provided a distraction.
